verifications.claim: Vaccines protect against influenza.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: high-dose flu vaccine; R6: Flu vaccine; R8: influenza; R9: Flu (influenza)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state vaccines protect against influenza/flu.

verifications.claim: Vaccines protect against COVID-19.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: COVID-19 vaccines; R6: COVID-19 vaccine; R9: COVID-19
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly mention COVID-19 vaccines providing protection.

verifications.claim: Vaccines protect against measles.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: measles vaccine; R6: MMR vaccine; R9: Measles; R11: measles vaccinations
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of measles vaccines in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Vaccines protect against HPV.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: HPV Vaccine, GARDASIL 9; R9: HPV (human papillomavirus)
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail HPV vaccines preventing related diseases.

verifications.claim: Vaccines are available at pharmacies, doctor's offices, and local health departments.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Vaccines are available at doctor's offices, most pharmacies and local health departments.
verifications.reasoning: Exact match in R11.

verifications.claim: Live-attenuated vaccines use weakened germs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: Live-attenuated vaccines use a weakened form of the germ; R2: Live attenuated bacteria and viruses
verifications.reasoning: Direct description matches claim precisely.

verifications.claim: Inactivated vaccines use killed germs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: Inactivated vaccines use a killed version of the germ; R2: Inactivated bacteria and viruses
verifications.reasoning: Precise terminology used in sources.

verifications.claim: Subunit vaccines use pieces of germs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: Subunit... vaccines use only specific pieces of the germ; R2: component (subunit) vaccines
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe subunit vaccines as using parts/pieces.

verifications.claim: MRNA vaccines provide instructions to make protein.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: mRNA vaccines use messenger RNA, which gives your cells instructions for how to make a protein
verifications.reasoning: Exact mechanism described.

verifications.claim: Viral vector vaccines are a vaccine technology.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: Viral vector vaccines use genetic material...; R2: adenovirus-based Ebola vaccine (Ad5-EBOV), viral vector
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm viral vector as a vaccine type/technology.

verifications.claim: Updated COVID-19 vaccines are available.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Updated COVID vaccines for approved groups are typically cleared
verifications.reasoning: R4 discusses updated COVID vaccines being available/cleared despite study halt.

verifications.claim: Specific formulations of COVID-19 vaccines are recommended for adults aged 65+.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Pfizer and BioNTech's Comirnaty... approved for adults aged 65 and older
verifications.reasoning: Specific approval for 65+ mentioned.

verifications.claim: Specific formulations of COVID-19 vaccines are recommended for those at higher risk.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: for younger people who are at higher risk of severe COVID-19
verifications.reasoning: Higher risk groups specified for recommendations.

verifications.claim: Annual flu vaccines are recommended.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: Children should receive flu vaccination every flu season
verifications.reasoning: Flu every season implies annual, but not explicitly 'annual flu vaccines' for all.

verifications.claim: High-dose flu vaccine options are often recommended for older adults.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: CDC recommends that all adults 65 years and older receive the high-dose vaccine
verifications.reasoning: Direct CDC recommendation for older adults.

verifications.claim: Routine immunizations for children and adults include diphtheria vaccine.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: Diphtheria Vaccination... People of all ages; R2: diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis... routine
verifications.reasoning: Routine for all ages including children and adults.

verifications.claim: Routine immunizations for children and adults include tetanus vaccine.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: Explicit for all ages.

verifications.claim: Routine immunizations for children and adults include pertussis (whooping cough) vaccine.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: CDC recommends whooping cough vaccination for people of all ages; R2: pertussis
verifications.reasoning: All ages routine.

verifications.claim: Routine immunizations for children and adults include polio vaccine.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: polio vaccine; R2: polio... routine immunization schedule
verifications.reasoning: Routine schedules include polio for children; adults via boosters implied.

verifications.claim: Routine immunizations for children and adults include MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R6: MMR vaccine 1st dose of 2 (for children 12-23 months)

verifications.claim: Vaccines prevent shingles.

verifications.claim: Vaccines prevent hepatitis B (liver cancer).

verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm prevention.
